clue.text: Religious type wanting hospital linked to church cause

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the hospital letter is taken away from the religious type

parts.note: a Hindu is a follower of Hinduism
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A believer leaves hospital to join a church cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked to' simply joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring about or prompt something is to cause it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Changing tune, pitied for lack of competence

indicators.note: changing means altering the order of the letters of the words given

explanation.surface: Pity for a poor musician who keeps changing the tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineptitude is clumsiness or incompetence, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Democrat raised morale, involving five hundred in scheme

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the reversed word wraps the Roman numeral
raised means turned upward, so in a down clue the word is read backwards

parts.note: ego is self-esteem, close to morale
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A politician boosts spirits with a costly plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or ruse, a crafty scheme.

clue.text: Sea with fish located earlier, being lucky

indicators.note: located earlier means the fish comes before the sea

parts.note: char is a trout-like fish
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A fortunate fisherman catches something at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word joining the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads a charmed life is lucky, protected as if by a spell.

clue.text: Seizing power, revolutionary goes for broke

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the turned word wraps round the power letter
revolutionary means turning round, so the word for goes is read backwards

parts.note: goes means leaves or departs
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A rebel grabs power and gambles everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing DEPARTS gives STRAPED; 'Seizing' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped for cash is slang for being short of money, the same as broke.

clue.text: Drone informally during start of meal

parts.note: thru is the informal, American spelling of through, which means during

indicators.note: start of means take only the first letter of the word meal

explanation.surface: Someone talks monotonously all through dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a continuous low humming sound, which is a drone.

clue.text: Claim with conclusion taken out and run over quickly

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, which is removed here

parts.note: to allege is to claim
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: An assertion is cut short and quickly passed over.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLEGE loses its last E, giving ALLEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction meaning to play at a brisk, lively pace.

clue.text: Comrade to receive love and shelter, I promise

indicators.note: to receive means the comrade word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a pal is a comrade or friend
O is love, a zero score in tennis
a tent is a simple shelter

explanation.surface: A friend is given love and a home, and swears to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster with promise has potential, future ability yet to be realised.

clue.text: Regime followed by slimmer assembly

definitions.meaning: an eating plan kept by someone trying to lose weight
a legislative assembly, such as the Japanese parliament or a historic German one

explanation.surface: A weight-loss plan followed by a thinner parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a restricted eating plan and a formal political assembly.

clue.text: Cave in wooded area swallowing everything up

indicators.note: swallowing means the woodland word takes the other inside

parts.note: a copse is a small wood

indicators.note: up means read upwards, so in a down clue the word is reversed

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A cave in a wood that gobbles up all that enters.
explanation.definitionFit: To cave in is to fall down or give way, the same as to collapse.

clue.text: Stop European support, not following enterprise

parts.note: to stop is to end

indicators.note: not here means without, so the letter for following is dropped

parts.note: to favour someone is to support them
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A call to halt European backing and not follow some business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an undertaking or venture, so enterprise in the sense of a project is a synonym.

clue.text: Settled on measure of capacity

parts.note: a bird that settled on a branch lit on it
RE means on or about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Something decided upon as a standard of volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of liquid volume, one thousand cubic centimetres, is a measure of capacity.

clue.text: Article furious about nation with mass detection technique

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the furious word goes round the nation and mass

parts.note: furious means raging
Mali is a West African nation
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece rages about some country and a large-scale method of finding things.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrared cameras that pick up heat from bodies form a method used to detect people or objects.

clue.text: Consistent record broken by university in the end

parts.note: even means steady or consistent

indicators.note: broken by means split open with the university letter put inside

parts.note: a tally is a running record or count

explanation.surface: A steady record is finally broken by a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means at last or finally, the same as in the end.

clue.text: Scandalous information turned round a secret society

indicators.note: round means the reversed scandal word goes around the letter a
turned means the word for scandal is written backwards

parts.note: dirt is gossip or scandal about someone

explanation.surface: Gossip that comes back to bite a clandestine group.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese criminal organisation of this name is a classic example of a secret society.

clue.text: Seek to keep old US city unspoiled

indicators.note: to keep means to hold, so the seek word contains the other pieces

parts.note: to invite trouble is to seek it
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Trying to preserve an old American city in pristine shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means untouched or kept intact, so unspoiled is a synonym.

clue.text: Sanction framed by academic that is against composer

indicators.note: framed by means surrounded by, so the approval word sits inside the academic

parts.note: a prof is a professor
to sanction is to OK something
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is
V stands for versus, against

explanation.surface: An approval set up by a professor turns out to oppose a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Prokofiev was a Russian writer of music, including Peter and the Wolf.

clue.text: Be quiet during act, missing right beat

indicators.note: during means the quiet word sits within the trimmed act
missing means lacking, so the right letter is removed

parts.note: a routine is a performer's act
sh is a call to be quiet

explanation.surface: A performer told to hush mid-act, losing the right rhythm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like a noun for rhythm, but it is the verb meaning to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine rivals is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: One pretending to be fouled by fellow showing disagreement

parts.note: in football a diver is a player who falls over to feign a foul
a gent is a gentleman or fellow

explanation.surface: A footballer faking a foul by another man causes an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Divergent views differ from one another, so they show disagreement.

clue.text: Revel in resistance, ordered to rise

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters of to rise are rearranged

explanation.surface: Enjoying a rebellion when the resistance is told to rise up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' looks like a reversal signal in a down clue, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to celebrate noisily and boisterously, which is to revel.

clue.text: In low area have look for criminal

indicators.note: in means the look word goes inside the low area

parts.note: a fen is low marshy ground, as in East Anglia
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone in a marshy spot takes a look round for a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A felon is someone who has committed a serious crime, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Lover, go on and flourish

parts.note: a fan is a lover of something, as in a music lover
to fare is to get on or go on, as in how did you fare

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is urged to carry on and thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish of trumpets is a short ceremonial musical call, the same as a fanfare.

clue.text: Resolved to hunt, hail hero exhibiting superior attitude

indicators.note: resolved read as re-solved, worked out again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hunter's tribute to a hero, seen as smug.
explanation.definitionFit: This hyphenated phrase describes someone sanctimonious who acts morally better than others, a superior attitude.

clue.text: Old letters in English among works

indicators.note: among means placed within, so the English letter goes inside

parts.note: a machine that works runs

explanation.surface: Ancient inscriptions turning up in English literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Runes are characters of an ancient Germanic alphabet, carved letters of old.

clue.text: Carnivore with yen approaching houses

indicators.note: houses means holds within, so the answer sits inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A hungry meat-eater nears some homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like part of the picture, but it signals the answer is held within with yen approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a meat-eating African mammal, an example of a carnivore.

clue.text: Upset at most awkward situation

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: tops means at most, as in ten pounds tops

explanation.surface: Being upset at most uncomfortable circumstances.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a spot, or a tight spot, means being in a difficult predicament.

clue.text: Mean temperature found

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it

explanation.surface: An average temperature reading has been discovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning to establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found a colony or institution is to establish or set it up, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Unrivalled forward, trim, inhibited by nothing

indicators.note: inhibited by means held in by, so the zero word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: nil means nothing or zero
on means forward, as in move on
to pare is to trim

explanation.surface: A striker without equal is held back by a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil means having no equal, matchless, so it fits unrivalled.

clue.text: Speculator in time before robbery having load of gold

indicators.note: before means the time letter comes ahead of the rest
having a load of means carrying, so the robbery word contains the gold

parts.note: a heist is a robbery
OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone who guesses about a raid that bagged a pile of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist forms hypotheses and so speculates about things.

clue.text: Empty country next to field covering good part of estate

indicators.note: next to means the two parts sit side by side
covering means the field word goes over the good letter

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word country is removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Land on a country estate, a field near a deserted nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bequest left in a will forms part of a dead person's estate.
